title: Check flake: the parity hostile-config test loops every fixture in one test (7 s under load)
description: DEC-299 (a5) item 2 follow-up from GCLI-55: test/parity.test.ts 'a hostile global config gives the same bytes' ran every fixture (three produceCodeMap calls and a fixture build each) inside ONE test and took 7.08 s under 20 busy loops (bun 1.3.14, junit durations, 60 s timeout), over bun's 5 s default by itself. Split into one test per fixture: the slowest is now 1.53 s; the assertions are unchanged. test/cli.test.ts 'every successful --json invocation emits its registry kind' (3.9 s under the same load) is reported, not changed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the hostile-config parity assertions run as one test per fixture with the same assertions (proof: bun test lists one test per fixture)
under 20 busy loops no test in the parity and stream files exceeds 3 s (60 percent of bun's 5 s default) over 3 runs (proof: junit durations recorded in the GCLI-63 notes)

implementationNotes: 2026-11-23 junit run (bun test parity+stream, 20 busy shell loops, dev 4cf670e plus GCLI-63 comment edits): slowest test 2.48 s (parity 'fallback is a true control: an absent index'), then flush proof 2.39 s, 2.30 s; every other test 2.03 s or less, so the AC bound (2.5 s) holds with 0.02 s to spare on the worst. Headroom to bun's 5 s default is about 2x; Check can still flake under heavier load. No timeout was raised. One test per command / per fixture is visible in the junit names.

AC2 restated 2026-11-23 on the Sonnet review of GCLI-63: bound 3 s, 3 runs. After splitting the two fallback-control loops one test per fixture (GCLI-63), the parity file's slowest test is 1.43 / 1.53 / 1.49 s under 20 busy loops. The earlier 2.48 s figure was the fallback-control loop (the 0.02 s margin).
finalSummary: Landed as glyph-cli#111; both ACs ticked, AC2 restated to the 3 s bound with timings recorded in GCLI-63.
